blocking.issue: validate_single_name enforces an ASCII [A-Za-z0-9._-] character allowlist, which makes the design's macOS canonical state chain impossible to create and makes the shared read primitive reject ordinary repository filenames. Structural single-component safety is not that allowlist.
blocking.location: src/ptest/files.py:24-26 (_COMPONENT_CHARS), :33-44 (validate_single_name), :47-57 (_split_relative, applied to every component of every relative path), :217-221 (ensure_shared_dir), :258-262 (ensure_private_dir), :299-307 (create_exclusive), :123-133 (read_regular)
blocking.evidence: _COMPONENT_CHARS = frozenset("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789._-") and validate_single_name raises Problem("unsafe-path", "name ... uses unsafe characters") for any other character, including SPACE and all non-ASCII. Design section 7 states verbatim: "macOS uses <account>/Library/Application Support/ptest/machine.toml" and "On first executing admission, T4 creates missing canonical shared-parent components one at a time via ensure_shared_dir: Linux .local->state->ptest and .config->ptest, or macOS Library->'Application Support'->ptest". Concrete failure: ensure_shared_dir(Path(account_home)/"Library", "Application Support") raises Problem unsafe-path before any mkdir, so on macOS the coordination root can never be created and every executing admission fails; macOS is in the user-approved v1 platform scope (.pipeline/context.md, design section 3). Second concrete failure: _split_relative validates every component with the same allowlist, so read_regular(root, "tests/test data/test_api.py", n) and read_regular(root, "app/routes/[slug].test.ts", n) both raise unsafe-path. Design section 9 requires source.py to fingerprint "tracked inputs, untracked candidates, declared ignored/generated inputs, native config/lockfiles and test roots" and section 10 requires doctor to scan "declared tests, conftest/fixture/setup files, runner/ptest config, then app sources" through exactly these descriptor-relative no-follow reads; bracketed and spaced filenames are routine in the Vitest/JS profile the design commits to. tests/ng/test_files.py contains no case for a name with a space, non-ASCII, or a bracket, so all 49 green tests pass over this gap.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: Task0 is the shared runnable barrier that freezes the file primitives every later task must consume without duplicating them ('T1/T3/T4/T8/T11/T13 consume these shared APIs; no independent unsafe writer/SQLite-opening implementation'). The frozen API contradicts the approved design's macOS canonical chain and cannot service the approved source/doctor scanning contract, so the barrier is not correct to hand to parallel writers; correcting it after wave 1 starts would require a shared-contract barrier repair across already-running tasks.
blocking.fix: Replace the character allowlist with the structural check the design actually specifies: reject non-str/empty, ".", "..", any "/" and any NUL, and (defensibly) other C0 control characters; accept every remaining byte sequence, including spaces and non-ASCII. Keep the existing O_NOFOLLOW/O_DIRECTORY descriptor-relative traversal as the real safety boundary. Add regression tests for ensure_shared_dir(parent, "Application Support") and read_regular over "test data/[slug].test.ts".

blocking.issue: _walk_to_parent leaks every intermediate directory descriptor on the SUCCESS path; only the error path closes them. Any relative path with two or more leading components leaks one FD per extra component per call.
blocking.location: src/ptest/files.py:74-111 (_walk_to_parent), consumed at :138-165 (read_regular finally block) and :313-351 (create_exclusive finally block)
blocking.evidence: In the loop, after opening `child`, the code does `if fd is not root_fd: opened.append(fd) else: opened.append(None)` and then `fd = child`; on normal completion it executes `return fd` and the `opened` list is discarded without closing anything. The `for item in opened: os.close(item)` cleanup lives only in `except Exception:`. Callers close exactly three descriptors: the final fd, parent_fd (when it differs from root_fd) and root_fd. Trace for read_regular(root, "src/pkg/mod.py", n): parts[:-1] = ["src","pkg"]; iteration 1 appends None and sets fd=fd_src; iteration 2 appends fd_src and sets fd=fd_pkg; returns fd_pkg. fd_src is never closed. tests/ng/test_files.py:32-38 is the only nested-success case and uses depth 2 ("sub/note.txt"), which leaks nothing, so the green suite cannot detect this. Consequence: design section 9 sizes the input envelope at up to 100,000 files read through this exact primitive; after roughly 1,000 nested reads the process hits the default RLIMIT_NOFILE and _open_dir's `except OSError` converts EMFILE into Problem("state-unavailable", "cannot open directory ..."), i.e. selection/doctor abort partway with a misleading state error and no bound is respected.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: 'Bounded memory/disk/scan growth' is an explicit approved acceptance priority and the brief requires tracing FD lifetime in the shared primitives. A resource leak in the one shared reader/writer that T3, T8, T11 and T13 are forbidden to reimplement fails the barrier, and the leak is invisible to the committed test suite.
blocking.fix: Close intermediate descriptors on the success path too: keep a list of the descriptors actually opened inside the loop (excluding root_fd), and in a `finally`/post-loop step close every one except the descriptor being returned. Add a test that calls read_regular repeatedly (e.g. 2,000 iterations) on a depth-3 relative path and asserts the open-descriptor count in /proc/self/fd (or resource-limit stability) does not grow.

blocking.issue: Decode entry points translate only ValueError/UnicodeDecodeError from json.loads, so deeply nested input raises an unhandled RecursionError instead of the declared typed rejection, and the declared nesting bound is never reached.
blocking.location: src/ptest/contracts.py:1847-1850 (decode_public_document), :1955-1958 (decode_control_frame), :2133-2139 (decode_launch_manifest), with _check_nesting at :1906-1916 applied only after parsing
blocking.evidence: Each decoder wraps json.loads in `except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError)` and only afterwards calls _check_nesting(..., CONTROL_FRAME_MAX_NESTING=16 / MANIFEST_MAX_NESTING=32). CPython's json parser raises RecursionError (not a ValueError) once nesting exceeds the interpreter recursion limit, which defaults to 1000. A 2,002-byte body of '['*1000 + ']'*1000 is far inside CONTROL_FRAME_MAX_BYTES=65536, so decode_control_frame propagates RecursionError to the guard/caller rather than Problem('protocol-mismatch'). Design section 6 requires 'Control frame max 65536 bytes, nesting<=16 ... Reject truncated/oversized/wrong-protocol/wrong-nonce frames with no execution', and the same hole exists for decode_public_document, which is the consumer-strict boundary for imported documents and --result-json artifacts. tests/ng/test_contracts.py exercises truncation, oversize, wrong protocol, wrong nonce and wrong kind shape, but no nesting case at all.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: Error truth and typed rejection at the protocol boundary are T0 acceptance items ('unknown-major/frame-truncation/wrong-nonce/oversize rejection'); an unhandled RecursionError in the guard channel is a crash path, not a rejection, and the advertised nesting bound is unenforceable as written.
blocking.fix: Catch RecursionError alongside ValueError/UnicodeDecodeError in all three decoders and map it to the same protocol-mismatch/report-invalid Problem, or pre-scan the raw bytes for bracket depth before parsing. Add negative tests asserting Problem for a frame and a public document nested past both the declared limit (16/32) and the interpreter recursion limit.
